message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑run **gcloud** command that will create a Compute Engine instance in Google Cloud with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you prefer the REST API or a Python client, see the sections below.)

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI command

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Pick a machine type that can host the GPU
#    n1-standard-8 has 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM – plenty for a single A6000
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 3. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=${MACHINE_TYPE} \
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: add a startup script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The Compute Engine zone (must support GPUs). |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk (SSD recommended). |
| `--boot-disk-type=pd-ssd` | Use SSD for better performance. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (adjust as needed). |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot. |

> **Prerequisites**  
> * Enable the **Compute Engine API** and **GPU API** in your project.  
> * Ensure **billing** is enabled and you have the necessary quota for GPUs in the chosen zone.  
> * Install the latest `gcloud` SDK (`gcloud components update`).  

---

## 2️⃣ REST API (HTTP) example

If you want to call the Compute Engine REST API directly, use the following POST request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "maintenancePolicy": "MIGRATE"
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values.  
The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically.

---

## 3️⃣ Python client (google-api-python-client)

```python
from googleapiclient import discovery
from oauth2client.client import GoogleCredentials

credentials = GoogleCredentials.get_application_default()
service = discovery.build('compute', 'v1', credentials=credentials)

project = 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID'
zone = 'us-central1-a'
instance_body = {
    'name': 'my-rtx-a6000',
    'machineType': f"projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
    'disks': [{
        'boot': True,
        'autoDelete': True,
        'initializeParams': {
            'sourceImage': 'projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts',
            'diskSizeGb': 100,
            'diskType': f"projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
        }
    }],
    'accelerators': [{
        'acceleratorCount': 1,
        'acceleratorType': f"projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }],
    'metadata': {
        'items': [{
            'key': 'startup-script',
            'value': '#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535'
        }]
    },
    'serviceAccounts': [{
        'email': 'default',
        'scopes': ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform']
    }],
    'maintenancePolicy': 'MIGRATE'
}

request = service.instances().insert(project=project, zone=zone, body=instance_body)
response = request.execute()
print(response)
```

---

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | GPU‑enabled zone selected |
| ✅ | Machine type supports the GPU |
| ✅ | GPU quota available |
| ✅ | Billing enabled |
| ✅ | Compute Engine & GPU APIs enabled |
| ✅ | Proper IAM permissions (e.g., `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`) |

Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh my-rtx-a6000@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
